transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Cypress Lead Eng), Alan Ruiz (Product), Nathan Park (CTO)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in focused on app integration, SDK patterns for function calling + structured outputs.

00:00 - Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, quick agenda — SDK integration notes, results from your test harness, structured output pain points, next steps.
00:18 - Maya: thanks, yeah we had a decent run last week, integrated the JS SDK into our staging service and tried the function-call flow for lab result parsing, but we saw a couple of issues.
00:31 - Ethan: ok can you describe the issues you hit? streaming, function calls, or the post-processing?
00:42 - Maya: the main thing was streaming — sometimes the JSON payload from the tool call comes in two chunks and our parser chokes, so we get malformed JSON. It looks like the SDK example didn't show the reassembly pattern clearly.
00:58 - Sofia: right, we had an example but it's a good call out. Ethan, there was that reassembly helper in the python/js SDKs, did we leave the streaming caveat in the docs?
01:09 - Ethan: we did but the example uses a naive split join; for the function-calls case we should be buffering until final=true or the finish token. I'll update the example to show an incremental parser that merges partial JSON. There's also a small bug where the client library emits the last chunk without the schema field when a callback is used — that's probably what you saw where the JSON is cut.
01:30 - Maya: yeah that sounds like it. Also, when we run higher QPS the latency spikes; our workflow is 2 RPCs per user transaction (prompt -> function call -> rerank) and we noticed 95th pctl jumps when batch sizes grow.
01:45 - Nathan: to add, cost matters — if dedicated capacity is required the monthly commit needs to make sense vs hosted. We're exploring dedicated if latency is stable.
01:56 - Sofia: totally, tradeoffs: dedicated gives predictability and VPC controls, hosted is cheaper for bursty. For the POC we can show a routing policy that pins critical endpoints to dedicated and sends lower priority to hosted — that might hit your SLA without full commit.
02:15 - Alan: can you also talk about structured output? we need strict JSON for downstream ingestion, and current outputs sometimes have trailing commas or missing fields.
02:27 - Ethan: yep this is a common one. Two levers: function-calling mode where the model returns a typed function call (name + args JSON), or response formatting with a strict JSON schema and post-parse validation. The function-call approach tends to be more reliable in our tests because the model is constrained.
02:45 - Maya: we tried function calling but occasionally the model still emits free text or adds commentary outside the JSON.
02:53 - Ethan: for that we recommend coupling function-calls with a lightweight JSON-schema validator on your side; additionally Redwood supports schema enforcement headers in the SDK — it's not a hard sandbox but it does increase the probability of valid outputs. We also have a retry policy option where the platform will automatically request a 2nd attempt if the returned payload fails schema validation.
03:18 - Nathan: are there any known interactions with quantization? we tested a quantized 8-bit model and saw a few hallucinations in numeric fields.
03:28 - Ethan: quantization can increase token-level noise, especially for precise numeric extraction. Our suggestion: keep your deterministic extraction models in higher-precision or use post-checks for numeric ranges. We can recommend per-model quantization profiles based on your token length distribution — Sofia will share the example profile.
03:45 - Sofia: I'll attach a recommended profile for common workloads (qa/parsing vs conversational) and an example config that uses smaller batch sizes for function-call endpoints to reduce tail latency.
03:58 - Maya: about security — we need KMS integration and audit logs; also want to understand if transient data is stored and for how long.
04:07 - Sofia: Redwood Private gives VPC + customer-managed KMS and you can configure retention. For hosted API, we have configurable retention windows and SOC2 controls. I'll send over the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide after the call.
04:25 - Alan: thanks. Also, in the SDK we saw an authentication token refresh edge case where long-running streams fail after token expiry.
04:34 - Ethan: that's a good catch — the SDK emits a reauth event but streaming reconnection is tricky. We can add a pattern in the examples that uses short-lived tokens with a reconnect helper. I'll patch the JS example to show graceful reconnect + checkpointing of partial function-call state.
04:56 - Maya: for the benchmark run — Ethan, can you run the 95th pctl for our nightly traffic shape? we instrumented the harness with sample user traces in the repo.
05:06 - Ethan: yes I'll run that and share a spreadsheet with p50/p90/p95 and cost per 1M tokens, including simulations for varying batch sizes.
05:16 - Nathan: and can you also show the model fallback path? if a dedicated pool is full, do requests fail or fallback to a hosted variant?
05:25 - Sofia: good question — we can set automated fallback to a compatible quantized variant in hosted to keep service online. We'll show a routing policy example in the follow-up demo.
05:37 - Alan: one more item — function-call latency: when the tool itself is an internal service, do you recommend synchronous tool calls or background async processing?
05:46 - Ethan: depends — synchronous is simpler but increases end-to-end latency; async with a callback can be more robust. For parsing tasks we often do sync if the function is cheap; for heavy enrichment we suggest function call that returns a job id and Redwood's structured output can include the job_id so your system can poll.
06:04 - Maya: we've started toggling batch size from 1 to 8 and saw cold-start latencies drop but p95 increased after a certain threshold. We need a recommended sweet spot.
06:15 - Ethan: we'll model it against your token distribution; initial recommendation is pkts of 2-4 for low latency workloads and 16+ for high throughput async jobs. I'll include a graph in the benchmark results.
06:28 - Sofia: quick check — are there any blocking legal/security items to proceed to the next pilot step?
06:34 - Nathan: we need the SOC2 summary & KMS doc, and network egress path details for dedicated/VPC. Otherwise good.
06:44 - Sofia: ok we'll get those over. Recap of outcomes: SDK streaming example to be updated, benchmark run scheduled, structured-output samples from Cypress, security docs shared, and follow-up demo for Dedicated/VPC routing.
06:58 - Maya: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround.
07:03 - Sofia: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.
